games.title: Raid on Bungeling Bay
games.note: Will Wright's helicopter shooter; he enjoyed building its islands in his map editor more than playing it.

games.title: SimCity 2000
games.note: Added an isometric view, hills, underground pipes and subways, and a newspaper reporting on your city.

games.title: Cities in Motion
games.note: Colossal Order's public transport sim, set in real cities such as Helsinki, Berlin, Vienna and Amsterdam.

games.title: Cities: Skylines
games.note: Made by a small team in Tampere, Finland; it became the leading city builder after SimCity (2013) disappointed.

games.title: Caesar
games.note: Build a Roman provincial city and its defenses to earn promotion toward emperor.

games.title: Caesar III
games.note: Citizens walk the streets to deliver services, so road layout decides whether houses get water, food and temples.

games.title: Pharaoh
games.note: Build Egyptian cities along the Nile, timing farms to the yearly flood and raising pyramids.

games.title: The Settlers
games.note: Volker Wertich's economy game where tiny settlers carry every log and fish along roads, one item at a time.

games.title: Anno 1602
games.note: An Austrian colony builder of island settlements and trade ships, a huge seller in German-speaking countries.

games.title: Populous
games.note: Raise and lower land so your followers can settle and multiply; widely considered the first god game.

games.title: Black & White
games.note: A god game with a giant creature that learns from how you reward and punish it.

games.title: Dungeon Keeper
games.note: You are the evil overlord: dig tunnels, keep monsters paid and happy, and crush the heroes who invade.

games.title: Transport Tycoon
games.note: Chris Sawyer wrote it in assembly language; Transport Tycoon Deluxe followed in 1995.

games.title: OpenTTD
games.note: A free, open-source remake of Transport Tycoon Deluxe that is still being updated.

games.title: RollerCoaster Tycoon
games.note: Sawyer wrote 99% of it in x86 assembly; for most of development it was called White Knuckle.

games.title: RollerCoaster Tycoon 3
games.note: The series' move to 3D, made by David Braben's Frontier with rides you can ride in first person.

games.title: Two Point Hospital
games.note: Two Point Studios was founded by Theme Hospital veterans Mark Webley and Gary Carr.

games.title: Little Computer People
games.note: A little man lives in a house inside your computer; you can talk to him, feed him and play cards.

links.took: Will Wright's map editor for building the game's islands, cities and roads.
links.added: Made building the city the whole game, with zones, budgets and simulated citizens.
links.extra: Wright found the editor more fun than the shooter itself.

links.took: Zoning, power, budgets and disasters.
links.added: An isometric view, terrain height, water pipes, subways and city ordinances.

links.took: Isometric city building with utilities and zoning.
links.added: Garbage management, neighbor deals and advisors who petition you.

links.took: Detailed city simulation with neighbor deals.
links.added: Regions of connected cities and 3D terrain you can sculpt.

links.took: The big, detailed SimCity-style city builder with zoning, traffic and utilities.
links.added: Huge maps, districts with their own policies and full support for player mods.
links.extra: Colossal Order wanted to move into a larger SimCity-style game; Wikipedia says it revived the SimCity style.

links.took: Colossal Order's traffic and public transport simulation, and its Unity engine work.
links.added: A whole city to zone and run, not just its buses and trams.

links.took: Profit-driven transport networks, a genre Transport Tycoon popularized.
links.added: Public transport inside real European cities across decades.

links.took: Large-scale city building with traffic, districts and mods.
links.added: A deeper economy, seasons and much larger buildable areas.
links.extra: It launched with serious performance problems.

links.took: SimCity's style of city building, including services such as schools and hospitals.
links.added: A Roman setting, military threats and promotion through ranks.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the Caesar games followed the style of SimCity over historical accuracy.

links.took: Roman city building with services and military threats.
links.added: Walkers who carry services along roads and a much more detailed economy.

links.took: Impressions' walker-based city engine and economy.
links.added: Ancient Egypt, the Nile flood cycle and monuments that take years to build.

links.took: Watching small people go about their lives inside the computer.
links.added: Hundreds of settlers working in a chain of jobs across a whole land.
links.extra: Volker Wertich named Little Computer People, Populous and SimCity.

links.took: A god-game view of a land and its busy little people.
links.added: Wertich dropped the god powers for an economy of production chains and carriers.

links.took: An open-ended simulation where you build and watch a settlement grow.
links.added: Goods carried by individual settlers and military expansion of borders.

links.took: Production chains, road networks and carriers.
links.added: A Roman campaign, ships and clearer graphics.

links.took: Production-chain economies that The Settlers made popular in German-speaking countries.
links.added: Island colonies, sea trade and population tiers that demand finer goods.

links.took: Island colony building, production chains and population tiers.
links.added: The Industrial Revolution, workforce classes, newspapers and expeditions.

links.took: Peter Molyneux's god game, where your power grows with your followers.
links.added: A giant creature you train, and miracles cast by mouse gestures.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Black & White was heavily influenced by the Populous series.

links.took: An all-powerful hand reaching into a world of tiny creatures.
links.added: Playing evil, digging a dungeon and managing monsters as an RTS hybrid.
links.extra: Both led by Peter Molyneux at Bullfrog.

links.took: Transport Tycoon Deluxe's game, rebuilt from reverse-engineered code.
links.added: Bigger maps, online multiplayer and two decades of community updates.
links.extra: Wikipedia and Maher note most modern players use OpenTTD.

links.took: Chris Sawyer's isometric management game and his assembly-language technology.
links.added: Building a theme park and designing roller coasters track piece by track piece.
links.extra: Sawyer chose a coaster game as his follow-up after visiting theme parks.

links.took: Running a theme park for profit, the genre Theme Park popularized.
links.added: Custom coasters built piece by piece and guests who react to every ride.

links.took: Coaster building and park management.
links.added: Scenario editor, more rides and themed scenery.

links.took: The coaster-building park sim.
links.added: Full 3D, rides you can ride in first person and firework shows.

links.took: Frontier's 3D theme park and coaster-building experience.
links.added: Free-form building with thousands of scenery pieces and online sharing.
links.extra: A spiritual successor to RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 from the same studio, made without the RollerCoaster Tycoon name.

links.took: Detailed 3D theme park and coaster building.
links.added: Water parks with pools and flumes, and console versions at launch.

links.took: Theme Hospital's comic hospital management, with silly diseases and staff to train.
links.added: A new world of Two Point County, more modern tools and themed hospitals.

src.t: PC Gamer, 'Prison Architect gave us the balls to make it'

links.extra: Made by Theme Hospital veterans Mark Webley and Gary Carr.

links.took: Two Point's humorous management and room-building.
links.added: Running a university, with courses, student lives and outdoor campuses.

links.took: The construction and management sim, which SimCity popularized.
links.added: A theme park with rides, shops, staff and visitors to please.
links.extra: Wikipedia says SimCity inspired a new genre of games.

links.took: Will Wright and Maxis's simulation design, zoomed from a city to one household.
links.added: Individual people with needs, moods and relationships in houses you build.

links.took: Watching and caring for little people living in a house on your screen.
links.added: Whole families you create, a house you build and needs you must manage.
links.extra: Often called a predecessor of The Sims; Will Wright mentioned getting feedback on The Sims from co-designer Rich Gold.

links.took: An isometric 3D look for Persson's early base-building prototype, RubyDung.
links.added: A first-person world of blocks to mine and build with.
links.extra: Wikipedia says RubyDung's perspective was similar to RollerCoaster Tycoon.

updates.why: First released in Japan as Dobutsu no Mori on the Nintendo 64 in April 2001.
